We've been constantly reminding everyone not to reveal sensitive personal information in conversations with AI chatbots, because most companies use those conversations as training data — but now there's an even more serious reason to be cautious.

The situation took a sharp turn for the worse over the weekend, when Reddit users discovered that certain Claude AI chat logs could be accessed through a simple Google search……

Claude Chat Content Leaked

Claude has a sharing feature that lets users share chat conversations with colleagues, friends, or family members. The chatbot generates a link that the user can send to one or more recipients, and Claude essentially assures users that anyone who knows the URL will not be able to view the conversation.

The problem is that Reddit users discovered that in reality, the link is not even needed to view the chats. Users simply had to search on Google — whether using specific keywords or asking Google to display all conversations shared this way. BBC News reported:

All you need to do is tell Google to search the directory used for sharing Claude chats (site:claude.ai/share), and you can easily obtain the relevant information.

As one might expect, some of the chats were quite outrageous — for instance, someone asking why the music industry was hiding the fact that most of Jay-Z's albums were co-written by birds. But other conversations contained extremely sensitive information, such as text transcripts of private conversations; a lawyer asking whether he needed to voluntarily report his own misconduct; and a user who, while asking for help setting up a cryptocurrency wallet, accidentally revealed their private key.

Anthropic is still trying to claim, to this day, that this is not a problem.

In reality, this is clearly a major problem, because it's entirely unexpected by users. What's worse, according to Wired, the root cause appears to lie in a serious lack of competence.

The incident came as news also broke yesterday that Claude Cowork was able to bypass sandbox restrictions on Mac and gain full access to all files.

How to Protect Yourself

The issue appears to have been at least partially addressed for now — search results that were previously obtainable can no longer be loaded — but given that the sharing feature relies on the principle of "security through obscurity," I would still advise everyone to avoid using it.

I would also recommend deleting all previously shared chat logs. Here's how: go to Settings > Privacy > Shared Chats > Manage.

Once Again Proving the Superiority of Apple's Approach

Apple Intelligence and the all-new Siri feature three layers of privacy protection:

  • Complete AI processing on-device wherever possible
  • The first fallback option is to use Apple's own Private Cloud Compute (PCC) servers
  • The final option is to use a Gemini model with equivalent PCC safeguards

The highly sophisticated PCC architecture means that neither Apple nor Google can ever access or retain any data. The security architecture Apple has designed can be verified by independent security researchers.
